kurals.tr: Vaalatrup Purkendra Kannum Avarsendra / Naalotrith Theyndha Viral
kurals.m: My finger has worn away by marking (on the wall) the days he has been absent while my eyes have lost their lustre and begin to fail

kurals.tr: Ilangizhaai Indru Marappinen Tholmel / Kalangazhiyum Kaarikai Neeththu
kurals.m: O you bright-jewelled maid, if I forget (him) today, my shoulders will lose their beauty even in the other life and make my bracelets loose

kurals.tr: Urannasaii Ullam Thunaiyaakach Chendraar / Varalnasaii Innum Ulen
kurals.m: I still live by longing for the arrival of him who has gone out of love for victory and with valour as his guide

kurals.tr: Kootiya Kaamam Pirindhaar Varavullik / Kotuko Terumen Nenju
kurals.m: My heart is rid of its sorrow and swells with rapture to think of my absent lover returning with his love

kurals.tr: Kaankaman Konkanaik Kannaarak Kantapin / Neengumen Mendhol Pasappu
kurals.m: May I look on my lover till I am satisfied and thereafter will vanish the sallowness of my slender shoulders

kurals.tr: Varukaman Konkan Orunaal Parukuvan / Paidhalnoi Ellaam Keta
kurals.m: May my husband return some day; and then will I enjoy (him) so as to destroy all this agonizing sorrow

kurals.tr: Pulappenkol Pulluven Kollo Kalappenkol / Kananna Kelir Viran
kurals.m: On the return of him who is as dear as my eyes, am I displeased or am I to embrace (him); or am I to do both?

kurals.tr: Vinaikalandhu Vendreeka Vendhan Manaikalandhu / Maalai Ayarkam Virundhu
kurals.m: Let the king fight and gain (victories); (but) let me be united to my wife and feast the evening

kurals.tr: Orunaal Ezhunaalpol Sellumsen Sendraar / Varunaalvaiththu Engu Pavarkku
kurals.m: To those who suffer waiting for the day of return of their distant lovers one day is as long as seven days

kurals.tr: Perinennaam Petrakkaal Ennaam Urinennaam / Ullam Utaindhukkak Kaal
kurals.m: After (my wife) has died of a broken heart, what good will there be if she is to receive me, has received me, or has even embraced me?
